pharm: Optimises cardiac energy metabolism by partially inhibiting fatty-acid oxidation, shifting myocardial energy production toward glucose, improving ischaemic tolerance.
quick: 35 mg modified-release twice daily, or 20 mg three times daily
Contraindicated in severe impairment (CrCl <30); reduce in moderate
summary: Trimetazidine is a metabolic anti-anginal agent used as add-on therapy for stable angina inadequately controlled by or intolerant to first-line anti-anginals. Rather than affecting heart rate or blood pressure, it improves myocardial energy efficiency during ischaemia by partially inhibiting fatty-acid oxidation. It can cause movement disorders, particularly parkinsonism, restless legs, tremor, and gait instability, which are reversible on stopping. It is contraindicated in Parkinson's disease and severe renal impairment. It is not approved by the US FDA.
indications: Add-on (second-line) symptomatic treatment of stable angina pectoris inadequately controlled by, or in patients intolerant of, first-line anti-anginal therapies
admin: Take with food, at meal times
Swallow modified-release tablets whole; do not crush or chew
Reassess benefit after about 3 months; discontinue if no response
Do not use to treat acute angina attacks (not a rescue medication)
Withdraw and review if movement or gait problems develop
moa: Trimetazidine partially inhibits the mitochondrial enzyme long-chain 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase, reducing fatty-acid beta-oxidation in cardiomyocytes. This shifts cardiac energy metabolism toward more oxygen-efficient glucose oxidation, preserving ATP production and intracellular pH and limiting calcium overload and free-radical damage during ischaemia. It improves myocardial energy metabolism without altering heart rate, blood pressure, or coronary blood flow (a 'cytoprotective' anti-anginal effect).

absolute: Parkinson's disease, parkinsonian symptoms, tremors, restless legs syndrome, and other related movement disorders
Severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min)
relative: Elderly (greater exposure; use lowest effective dose)
monitor: Gait instability and falls, especially in the elderly

preg: Not recommended; there are no adequate data on use in pregnancy. Avoid unless clearly necessary and no safer alternative exists.
lact: Avoid during breastfeeding; it is not known whether trimetazidine is excreted into human milk.
renal: Contraindicated in severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min). In moderate impairment (CrCl 30-60 mL/min) reduce to 35 mg modified-release once daily in the morning, as the drug is renally eliminated and accumulates.
hepatic: Use with caution in severe hepatic impairment; limited data are available.

moderate: Drugs that can cause or worsen extrapyramidal symptoms (additive movement-disorder risk)
minor: No clinically significant pharmacokinetic interactions established
interactions.food: Take with food; no specific food interaction of concern.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction documented; general caution advised.

serious: Parkinsonian symptoms (tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, gait instability)

monitoring: Movement disorders and gait at each review (especially elderly)
Symptom control and need to continue (reassess at ~3 months)
Signs of blood dyscrasia or hepatitis if symptomatic
counsel: This is an add-on medicine for angina prevention, not for treating sudden chest pain
Take it with your meals and swallow modified-release tablets whole
Tell your doctor if you develop tremor, stiffness, slowness, restless legs, or unsteadiness
Do not stop suddenly without advice; report fainting or unusual bruising
Continue your other heart medicines as prescribed
pk: Symptomatic anti-anginal benefit develops over days to weeks
Store at room temperature; protect from moisture
pearls: Metabolic anti-anginal - improves ischaemic tolerance without changing heart rate or blood pressure
Contraindicated in Parkinson's disease and movement disorders; can itself cause reversible parkinsonism and gait disturbance
Contraindicated in severe renal impairment; reduce dose in moderate impairment and the elderly
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your usual schedule - do not take a double dose.
overdose: Experience is limited. Overdose may cause hypotension and gastrointestinal symptoms. There is no specific antidote; treatment is supportive and symptomatic with monitoring of blood pressure and clinical status.
